newsitem.title: UK: Brit Gas, Shell no comment on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Brit Gas, Shell no comment on merger talk.

text.p: British Gas and oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group declined to comment on Sunday on a newspaper report saying the two firms were in merger talks.
"We do not comment on market rumours," said a British Gas spokeswoman. A Shell spokesman said the same.
The Sunday Telegraph reported that British Gas, privatised 10 years ago, had been approached by Royal Dutch/Shell with plans for a 40 billion pound ($66.6 billion) mega-merger.
But the paper added that the plans were said to have "gone cold because British Gas got cold feet".
The Sunday Telegraph said the Anglo-Dutch oil group, one of the world's biggest companies, had earlier prepared secret documents detailing a proposed takeover of British Gas.

The report comes after months of lingering stock market rumours that either British Petroleum or Royal/Dutch Shell are considering taking over British Gas, which plans to split itself in two early next year.
The utility wants to demerge into a pipeline firm, to be called TransCo International, and a gas trading company called British Gas Energy.
As the trading operations are lossmaking and the profitable pipeline business strictly regulated, many industry analysts have been sceptical about any takeover interest from BP or Shell.

But the Sunday Telegraph said Shell is thought to be particularly interested in British Gas's gas production operations, which are scheduled to be split between TransCo International and British Gas Energy.
